Your store, explained.

This guide covers every page of the new SpeakOut Wireless store: what each page does, how it was built, what you can edit yourself, and the rules the store enforces for you. Written for the 7-Eleven and Ztar teams by Makro.

Before launch The store lives at 7-eleven-17155.myshopify.com and is password protected while we finish: the password is MakroxSpeakout. Every link in this guide opens the live page in a new tab.

Three ways to use this guide:

  • Touring the build: read top to bottom. Each chapter shows the page and explains it.
  • Editing something: jump to the page's chapter and look for the blue "You can edit" card, then see Editing any page for the click-by-click method.
  • Testing (UAT): use the chapters as your checklist of what to try, and report anything that looks wrong with the feedback button. See Reporting feedback.
Start here

How the store thinks.

Five rules run through everything. Once you know them, every page makes sense.

1. Province first

The customer picks their province once, on the plans page or on a plan's own page. That choice follows them everywhere: it sets the provincial 911 fee, it rides into the cart, and it carries into activation. Provinces on offer are controlled by Ztar's systems together with the fee setup in Shopify.

2. One plan per order

A cart holds exactly one plan. Adding a different plan replaces the one that's there, along with its fee. Quantities are locked to one. The store cleans this up automatically, so a customer can never buy two plans in one order by accident.

3. The 911 fee is automatic

Every plan is paired with the government-mandated E911 fee for the customer's province, at the exact amounts Ztar provided. The fee adds itself, updates itself when the province changes, removes itself with the plan, and cannot be bought or removed on its own. Annual plans collect the whole year's fee at once.

4. The phone check talks to Ztar live

When a customer brings their own phone, the store sends the phone's IMEI to Ztar's device-check service the moment it's typed. Compatible phones get a green confirmation. A phone Ztar can't confirm gets an honest note and may continue. An incompatible phone is stopped. The store never guesses: it shows exactly what Ztar's service answers.

5. Buying and activating are two steps

Checkout pays for the plan. Activation, on its own page, is what turns the SIM on: it talks to Ztar's activation service and comes back with the customer's new phone number. The customer signs in with an email code first, so the activation is tied to their account.

Shopping

Homepage

Open the live page

The front door: hero, the plan grid pulled live from your plan lineup, the annual plan promotion, this month's deal, trust points, and customer reviews. Nothing on it is hard-coded: the plans shown are whatever is in the plan collections, and the deal band is a text setting.

Homepage, top portion. The plan cards come straight from the live catalog.
You can edit Every section: hero image or video and its text, the deal-of-the-month wording, which collections feed the plan grids, the reviews, the icon rows, the footer. All through the theme editor, no code. See Editing any page.
Good to know The reviews section currently shows placeholder quotes. Swap in real customer quotes in the theme editor when you have them. The reviews carousel supports trackpad swiping as well as the arrows.
Shopping

Plans page

Open the live page

The whole lineup on one page: six monthly plans, the annual plan, the current deal, and the province selector that drives everything. The customer also chooses their path here: "I have a phone" or "I need a SIM".

Plans page: province selector, deal band, monthly grid, annual grid.

How it behaves

  • Province selector: sets the province for the whole visit. Quebec is deliberately not offered; the list follows Ztar's supported provinces.
  • "I have a phone" + Add now: sends the customer to the plan's own page, where the phone check lives, with their province carried along.
  • "I need a SIM" + Add now: adds the plan straight to the cart with the right 911 fee paired. The button confirms with "Added" and the cart count updates.
  • Best Deal flag: lives on the plan product itself, so it moves when you flag a different plan. Only one plan carries it at a time.
  • Annual grid: fed by its own collection; the annual card charges the full year's 911 fee, correctly.
You can edit Headings, the deals band text and link, the helper line, which collections feed each grid, and the "included with every plan" strip. The plan cards themselves (price, data allowance, feature ticks, Best Deal flag) are edited on the plan products: see Products, plans and fees.
Shopping

Plan product page

Open a live example

Where a plan gets configured before it goes in the cart. The left side sells the plan; the right side walks the customer through four steps: province, phone, SIM, and what you pay today.

The plan page's "Set up your plan" panel: province, IMEI check, SIM choice, pay today.

How it behaves

  • Your province: preselected if the customer chose one earlier. The helper explains the 911 fee. Picking an unavailable province states that plainly and holds the add button.
  • Your phone: the IMEI field checks the phone against Ztar's service as soon as 15 digits are typed. Green means confirmed compatible. An amber note means Ztar couldn't confirm; the customer may continue. A red stop means the phone won't work. A wrong-length entry is told it needs 15 digits.
  • Your SIM: "I already have one" (bought at a 7-Eleven) or "Ship me a SIM", which adds the SIM item to the order.
  • What you pay today: live math: plan price plus the provincial 911 fee, updating as the province changes.
  • Add to cart stays off until the steps above are satisfied.
You can edit The plan's price, title, data allowance and feature list (on the product, see Products, plans and fees), the "How billing works" copy, helper lines, and the switching note, all in the theme editor.
Good to know While Ztar's device data feed is returning "unknown" for all phones, every IMEI shows the amber note. The green confirmation starts appearing automatically the moment their feed is fixed; nothing needs changing on the store.

Cart and checkout

Open the live page

The cart shows the plan with its province, the 911 fee as its own explained line, the SIM status, and an order summary that matches what checkout will charge. It also enforces the rules, politely.

Cart with a plan whose phone check came back unconfirmed: the note stays visible, checkout stays open.
Cart with a plan that skipped the phone check entirely: checkout is blocked until the IMEI is verified or a SIM is added.

The rules it enforces

  • One plan, quantity one. A second plan replaces the first. Quantities can't be raised.
  • The fee is untouchable. The 911 fee line explains itself and has no remove link. Removing the plan removes its fee with it.
  • IMEI gate. A bring-your-own-phone order that never ran the phone check shows "IMEI check incomplete" and keeps Checkout off. A check that ran but came back unconfirmed keeps Checkout open with a clear note. Adding a SIM lifts the gate, since a shipped SIM has no phone to verify yet.
  • Province gate. A plan tied to an unsupported province ("Quebec - Service unavailable") blocks checkout until the province is updated.
  • Account required. Plan checkouts route the customer through account creation, so the activation that follows has an owner.
Good to know Orders carry Ztar's own plan products plus a small set of order attributes (province, intent, IMEI, check result) that Ztar's fulfilment reads directly. That contract is agreed with Ztar; see Products, plans and fees for what never to rename.

Activation

Activating a SIM

Open the live page

The step that turns a SIM into a working phone number. It is a two-page flow connected live to Ztar's activation service.

Step one: activation code or SIM number, plus province. The voucher path hands off to the account portal.
The activation form is behind sign-in: an email code, no password to remember.

The flow

The customer enters the activation code from their SIM package (9 characters) or the SIM number itself (19 to 20 digits), picks their province, and continues. Bad input is caught immediately.
They sign in with their email and a 6-digit code. New customers are creating their account in the same step.
The form asks for their city (the list comes live from Ztar for that province), address, phone IMEI (checked live, same as on the plan page), and a 4-digit account PIN.
Activate submits to Ztar. Success shows "You're connected." with the new phone number, straight from Ztar's response, and a button to their account. A failure keeps everything they typed and asks them to try again.
Good to know The account button will point at the Ztar account portal once its web address is confirmed; autopay and plan management live there, after activation. City lists exist only for provinces Ztar has provisioned; provinces without them cannot complete activation, which is being aligned with Ztar.
Working the store

Editing any page

One method covers ninety percent of edits. Nothing here requires code, and nothing you do in the editor can break the buying logic.

In Shopify admin, go to Online Store → Themes and press Customize on the live theme. Or use the direct door: open the theme editor.
Use the dropdown at the top center to pick the page you want (Home page, Pages → Coverage, Collections → Plans, and so on). The editor shows the page exactly as customers see it.
Click any section on the page. Its settings open on the right: text, images, links, colours, toggles. Blocks inside a section (a single FAQ question, a single icon card) are listed on the left and edited the same way.
Press Save, top right. The change is live immediately. There is no separate publish step.
To editGo to
Homepage sectionsTheme editor → Home page
Plans page copy and deal bandTheme editor → Collections → Monthly plans
Why / Coverage / Switch / Deals / HelpTheme editor → Pages → pick the page
Menu links (header and footer)Admin → Content → Menus

Plan prices, names, Best Deal flagAdmin → Products (see next chapter)
Working the store

Products, plans and fees

The catalog has three kinds of citizens. Two are yours to edit freely. One set is load-bearing: it makes the Ztar integration work, and it should only change by agreement.

Plan pages: edit freely

Each plan the customer sees (500 MB plan, 1 GB plan, and so on) is a product of type "Plan page". Its price, title, data allowance, feature ticks, billing period and Best Deal flag live on the product and its metafields. Change a price or flag a different Best Deal here and every page updates.

Phones and accessories: edit freely

Normal Shopify products. Add, price and photograph them the standard way.

The load-bearing set: change only by agreement

ItemWhat it doesSafe to edit?
"Unlimited Talk & Text Plan" productZtar's own product. Its variants are what orders actually carry, so Ztar's systems can read every order.Ztar only
"E911 Fees" productOne variant per province at the government amounts, plus annual variants. Feeds the automatic fee pairing.By agreement
Province entries (metaobjects)Which provinces are offered, their names, and which fee variant each uses.By agreement
Plan metafields starting with speakout.Connect each plan page to Ztar's variant, its allowance text, billing period and flags.By agreement
Order attribute and property names (intent, billingProvince, imei, _speakout_...)The agreed contract Ztar reads off every order.Never rename
One rule to remember Changing a plan's price or copy is always safe. Deleting products, editing the fee product, or renaming anything technical is not: ask Makro or Ztar first, it takes minutes to check.
Working the store

Creating products

Three recipes: a new plan, a new phone, a new accessory. For plans and phones the fastest and safest method is the same one we use: duplicate one that works, then change what differs.

Create a new plan

Coordinate with Ztar first. Every plan the customer buys maps to a variant on Ztar's own plan product, so their systems can bill and fulfil it. If Ztar hasn't created the matching variant yet, the new plan has nothing to connect to. One message before you start saves the round trip.
In admin → Products, open an existing plan (say, 5 GB plan) and press Duplicate, top right. Keep images ticked. The duplicate arrives as a draft with everything carried over: the right template, the right product type ("Plan page"), and all the plan settings.
Change the basics: title (for example "10 GB plan"), and the price on the variant.
Scroll to Metafields at the bottom of the product page and update: Data allowance (the line under the price, for example "10 GB at 4G speed"), Included features (the tick list), Billing period (monthly or annual), and make sure Best deal is off, since only one plan carries the flag. The Ztar variant metafield is the connection from step 1: pick the matching variant on the "Unlimited Talk & Text Plan" product, or ask Makro to map it.
Under Collections on the right, add it to Monthly plans (or Annual plans). To control where it sits in the grid, open the collection and drag it into position, since the plan grid follows the collection's manual order.
Set status to Active and check the plans page: the new card should be there with its price, allowance and ticks, and adding it to the cart should pair the right 911 fee.

Create a new phone

Duplicate the existing phone product, or start fresh with Add product. Either way: title, description, and good photos (the first image is the collection card).
Leave "Product type" empty for phones. A few special type names (plan, Plan page, Fees, SIM) switch on special cart behavior, so a phone should not carry any of them.
Colours are variants: under Variants, add an option called Color and list the colours. Each colour can have its own price, image and inventory.
Set the price and inventory per variant, and tick "Track quantity" so a sold-out colour shows as unavailable.
Add it to the Phones collection under Collections on the right, set status to Active, and open the phones page to see it. Its own page automatically offers the plan pairing and SIM option, that comes with the phone template.

Create a new accessory

Add product: title, description, photos, price, inventory. No special settings, and again leave "Product type" empty.
Add it to the Accessories collection, set status to Active, and it appears on the accessories page.
The one trap Product type is not a label here, it is wiring. "Plan page", "plan", "Fees" and "SIM" each trigger store logic (fee pairing, one-per-order rules, purchase locks). Never type those into a phone or accessory, and never remove them from a plan. When in doubt, duplicate something that already works.
A safe way to practice Create anything as a Draft first: drafts are invisible to customers. Use the product page's Preview to check it, then flip to Active when it looks right.
Working the store

Reporting feedback

During testing, the fastest way to report anything is directly on the page where you see it.

Browse the store normally. A feedback button sits at the edge of every page.
See something wrong, or something you want changed? Press it. It takes a screenshot of exactly what you see.
Draw on the screenshot to point at the issue, write one or two sentences (what you did, what you expected), and send.
The report lands on the project board with the page, browser and console details attached automatically, so the team can reproduce it without back-and-forth. You'll be notified when it's resolved.
Good to know One report per issue works best. Change requests and new ideas are welcome through the same button; the team triages them separately from bugs.
